public_rationale: The evidence points both ways and nothing measures the net effect. UK freedom-of-information data show proven AI cheating rose from 1.6 to 5.1 cases per 1,000 students between 2022-23 and 2023-24, and experts say that is the tip of the iceberg. A large US study warns that misuse threatens assessment validity. That supports damage to assessment integrity. On the other hand, a randomized trial at Harvard found college students learned significantly more with an LLM-based tutor. So LLMs are not uniformly harmful to college learning. Marcus gives the point as a passing example, and 'undermined' is not defined. No study establishes an overall decline in college education caused by LLMs.
limitations: The supporting evidence is mostly about cheating, not learning outcomes.
The contradicting RCT is small and uses a custom tool.
